title: Effect Oriented Programming
byline: Bill Frasure, Bruce Eckel and James Ward · Scala 3 and ZIO 2
note: Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: An introduction to effect systems for working programmers, using Scala 3 and ZIO. An effect is any unpredictable interaction with the outside world (clocks, files, networks, randomness, mutation); wrapping effects as values that describe work instead of doing it gives back control. The book shows what that buys: retries, timeouts, fallbacks and finalizers added without changing the code they wrap; dependencies modeled as layers and wired into a graph; deterministic tests with controllable clocks and randomness; typed failures in place of thrown exceptions; composition with existing Scala types; safe shared state; and resilience patterns such as caching, rate limiting, circuit breaking and hedged requests.
